audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL internals (EVM environment opcodes, SSTORE gas metering, BLAKE2 precompile, PoW difficulty/rewards, Prague fork types including EIP-7702 authorizations) and CL internals (Deneb fork state upgrade, blob gas initialization). Wallet/provider EIPs (EIP-7039, EIP-2786) are also present but primarily describe client-side interfaces.

in_scope: EVM Environment Opcodes (BALANCE, CALLDATALOAD, RETURNDATACOPY, BLOBHASH)
Prague Fork Types (Account, Authorization for EIP-7702)

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via gas manipulation, EIP-7702 authorization forgery attempts
Eclipse attacks, propagate invalid blocks with incorrect difficulty or rewards, send blocks that exploit gas metering edge cases

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid blob gas fields during Deneb fork transition
Provide incorrect state during fork transitions, serve malformed execution payloads

misclassified_entities.reason: Block Processor is an internal node component executing state transitions, not an external entity. It resides within the system boundary.
Contract Execution Context is the internal EVM execution engine, not an external entity. The actual external entity is the transaction submitter who provides the bytecode.
EVM Precompile Caller represents internal EVM execution calling a precompile. The actual external entity is the transaction submitter whose transaction triggers the precompile call.
Same as EXT-EVM-PRECOMPILE — internal EVM context, not an external entity.
Provider State Change is an internal event trigger within the provider, not an external entity.
EIP-5069 is a Meta EIP defining editor governance. Editor Candidate is not relevant to protocol runtime security.
EIP-5069 is a Meta EIP defining editor governance. Keeper of Consensus is not relevant to protocol runtime security.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Sender)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_sendRawTransaction RPC — provides call data, blob versioned hashes, EIP-7702 authorizations
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated user input via public JSON-RPC. All transaction data (call data, blob hashes, authorization tuples) is attacker-controlled. Covers EXT-TRANSACTION-SENDER, EXT-BLOB-TX-SUBMITTER, and EXT-TRANSACTION-SUBMITTER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Potentially Reentering Call via EVM
trusted_external_entities.rationale: An internal call frame initiated by attacker-controlled contract code. The call may attempt SSTORE with only stipend gas to exploit reentrancy. Untrusted because the calling contract is user-deployed.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated network peer. Can send blocks with invalid difficulty, incorrect rewards, or malformed headers. Covers EXT-P2P-NETWORK, EXT-PEER, EXT-MINER, EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: External Data Source via RPC/P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: RLP-decoded data entering type validation (Address, Root, Bloom)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any external source providing byte data that must pass type validation boundaries. Untrusted because data may arrive from P2P or RPC without authentication.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Provider via web+evm:// Protocol Handler
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Wallet provider communicates via browser message passing. No authentication of provider identity beyond protocol handler registration. A malicious extension could register the handler.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Provider injection into web page (window.ethereum, EIP-2786)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extension injects provider object. User implicitly trusts via installation, but from the DApp's perspective, the injected provider is untrusted — it could be malicious or spoofed.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Client via Provider API
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EIP-2700 listener attachment and RPC requests (EIP-2786)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApp attaches listeners to the provider. From the wallet's perspective, the DApp is untrusted and may attempt to extract sensitive data or phish the user.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blockchain Network (connectivity)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Network reachability is not authenticated. A MITM or eclipse attack could fake connectivity status, causing incorrect connect/disconnect events.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Call data bytes are entirely attacker-controlled. buffer_read must correctly zero-pad out-of-bounds reads. Memory expansion gas must be charged before copy.

Blob versioned hashes are provided by the transaction submitter. Index bounds must be checked; out-of-bounds returns zero. blob_versioned_hashes list integrity must be validated during transaction decoding.
Authorization chain_id, signature (y_parity, r, s), and nonce must all be validated. ECDSA signature recovery must be correct. Invalid authorizations must be rejected without side effects.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM SSTORE opcode (EIP-2200 gas stipend check)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: gasleft must be strictly greater than 2300 for SSTORE to proceed. This prevents reentering calls with only stipend gas from modifying state. The boundary condition (> not >=) must be exact.

Full block validation required: difficulty must match expected calculation (with bomb delay offset), PoW must verify against difficulty target, block rewards must match 2 ETH base (post-Constantinople). Invalid blocks must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Prague fork type validation (Address/Bytes20, Root/Hash32, Bloom/Bytes256)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All incoming byte data must pass length validation before being cast to typed values. Exactly 20 bytes for Address, 32 bytes for Root, 256 bytes for Bloom. Rejection on mismatch.

Message origin must be validated. Response must have exactly one of result or error. Provider info (name, icon) must be sanitized before rendering to prevent XSS. Multiple wallet responses must be handled safely.
DApps should not blindly trust the injected provider. The provider could emit false connect/disconnect events or return incorrect chainId. DApps must validate critical data independently.
Wallet must not leak sensitive data to arbitrary DApp listeners. Listener callback exceptions must not crash the provider. Event data must not include private keys or signing material.
Connect/disconnect events are derived from network state which can be manipulated. DApps must handle rapid state transitions gracefully and not assume persistent connectivity.

coverage_analysis.notes: 7 entities from source files were reclassified as misclassified (internal components or non-runtime governance). EIP-5069 (Meta EIP) and Deneb fork upgrade (no external entities in subgraphs) do not contribute external entities. Deneb fork is an internal state transition triggered at epoch boundary with no external data ingress in these subgraphs.
